item.research_question: Can a multiobjective Bayesian optimization framework be used to discover high entropy alloy electrocatalysts with balanced catalytic activity, cost-effectiveness, and entropic stabilization in vast composition spaces?
item.material_system: High entropy alloys (HEAs) composed of up to 10 elements (Ag, Au, Cu, Ir, Os, Pd, Pt, Re, Rh, and Ru)
key_findings: The multiobjective BO framework can efficiently identify promising HEA electrocatalysts with balanced properties
The framework can handle high-dimensional design spaces with up to 10 elements
The identified optimal HEAs achieve a balance among catalytic activity, cost-effectiveness, and entropic stabilization
The framework is data-efficient, requiring only 50-140 evaluations to reach 95% of the maximum hypervolume indicator
The framework can be used to explore different regions of the compositional landscape and identify diverse promising candidates
item.mechanism: The framework uses a diversity-guided batch selection strategy and a Gaussian process regression (GPR) surrogate model to explore the design space and predict the catalytic activity of arbitrary HEAs
item.limitations: The simplified assumption of the surface model, which may not be completely accurate for describing the true catalyst surface
item.future_work: Improving the surface model by developing a better ML model for phase prediction and further experimental characterization
quotes: we have developed a data-efficient multiobjective BO framework tailored for the discovery of HEA electrocatalysts for ORR
the identified optimal binary to quinary HEAs are supported by previous experimental results, whereas those with more elements are awaiting experimental validation

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a multiobjective Bayesian optimization framework be used to discover high entropy alloy electrocatalysts with balanced catalytic activity, cost-effectiveness, and entropic stabilization in vast composition spaces?. System: High entropy alloys (HEAs) composed of up to 10 elements (Ag, Au, Cu, Ir, Os, Pd, Pt, Re, Rh, and Ru). Findings: The multiobjective BO framework can efficiently identify promising HEA electrocatalysts with balanced properties; The framework can handle high-dimensional design spaces with up to 10 elements; The identified optimal HEAs achieve a balance among catalytic activity, cost-effectiveness, and entropic stabilization; The framework is data-efficient, requiring only 50-140 evaluations to reach 95% of the maximum hypervolume indicator; The framework can be used to explore different regions of the compositional landscape and identify diverse promising candidates. Mechanism: The framework uses a diversity-guided batch selection strategy and a Gaussian process regression (GPR) surrogate model to explore the design space and predict the catalytic activity of arbitrary HEAs. Limitations: The simplified assumption of the surface model, which may not be completely accurate for describing the true catalyst surface. Future work: Improving the surface model by developing a better ML model for phase prediction and further experimental characterization. Quote: "we have developed a data-efficient multiobjective BO framework tailored for the discovery of HEA electrocatalysts for ORR"
